nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.

A model generated during the first pass analysis based on message folder placement and message attributes, used to score and identify misclassified messages; it resides exclusively in non-persistent memory and is purged after use.

A message filter used to sort messages into different message folders and configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that sorts messages into different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of user action.
A filter configured to generate a classification model from a first pass analysis and use it in a second pass to generate misclassification identification of sorted messages.

A device distinct from a client device on which the first message filter is configured to execute.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform multi-pass message filtering actions.<SEP>A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network to the message folders.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first and second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.

A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass filter.<SEP>Different folders into which messages are sorted; a message may be identified as sorted into an incorrect message folder and moved to another folder by a user.
A generated identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, displayed so a user can move misclassified messages to a different folder.
A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, not stored on disk or another persistent data store, and from which it is purged.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

A storage medium storing processor readable instructions relating to the multi-pass message filter and message management.<SEP>A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

A device on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and where the first and second passes may occur entirely.<SEP>A device on which the multi-pass message filter is executed, where second classification data resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and is deleted upon providing the display of information.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including sender address and whether the sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.
Header information within messages, including a subject, read during the first pass analysis.
A network address from which a message originates, read during the first pass analysis.
The content of messages read during the first pass analysis.
Files attached to messages, read during the first pass analysis.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis of message senders.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in the address book is one basis for generating second classification data.
Unwanted email messages that the filtering approach aims to identify and filter.

A message filtering system that executes a first pass and a second pass to classify messages, optionally employing a Naive Bayes classifier.<SEP>A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message.
A classifier that the multi-pass message filter may employ.
Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.<SEP>Classification data generated and stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.

Classification data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter, and which can be deleted so it is no longer accessible.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train it; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and is deleted upon providing the display of information.
A model generated based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted and in which a message currently resides.

A method for managing message delivery that includes receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a first pass of a multi-pass message filter on a client device.
A memory store on the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A plurality of messages received, sorted into message folders, and scored by the multi-pass message filter.
A communications network over which the network device communicates messages to the message folders.
A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and able to select the multi-pass message filter for execution through an interface on the client device.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.
A header of a message, used as a basis for generating second classification data.
The content of a message, used as a basis for generating second classification data.
A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to identify messages sorted into an incorrect message folder.
